summary: The manuscript presents a machine-checked Lean 4.35.0 formalization (18 constructive theorems, zero external dependencies, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 3 zero-axiom theorems) and a pure-stdlib exact-Q Python certificate auditor (BOOTSTRAP-TOWER-CERT-1.0) covering the finite algebraic, d-closed barrier, exact rational outward-witness binomial tail w_0, and finite-scale geometric core of Koval and Peres's majority bootstrap percolation tower transition (arXiv:2611.33087). All mathematical derivations, exact rational filling probabilities on Z_3^2 vs [3]^2, Z_4^3 barrier-closure censuses, binomial tail values, and table/figure statistics visible in the PDF are internally consistent and independently check out. The authors explicitly and accurately scope their work away from the asymptotic probabilistic concentration and multi-scale renormalization arguments of Koval and Peres, leaving no unresolved material objections.
weaknesses: As a 4-page summary paper, the PDF prints Lean theorem identifiers, axiom footprints (Table 1), and high-level prose summaries (Proposition 1) rather than the formal Lean type signatures or certificate schemas themselves, so verification of exact formal specifications relies on the external repository.

The formalization addresses only the elementary deterministic, algebraic, and finite-graph components of [5] and does not formalize the probabilistic couplings, concentration bounds, or renormalization proofs underlying Theorem 1.1 and Eq. (1.2).
Verifier bounds in Mode 2 (|V| <= 256) and Mode 3 (4 <= d <= 32, den(p) <= 1000) restrict certified instances to small finite lattices and moderate dimensions.
